lessons.title: Eid
lessons.goal: Greet people at Eid and talk about Eid customs.
grammar: locative / genitive of ঈদ: ঈদে 'at Eid', ঈদের দিন 'on Eid day'
lessons.tip:
Bangladesh celebrates two Eids: **ঈদুল ফিতর** at the end of Ramadan and **ঈদুল আজহা** (the festival of sacrifice). The greeting for both is **ঈদ মোবারক!** — reply with the same.

Eid morning: men go to the Eid prayer (**ঈদের নামাজ**), everyone wears **নতুন** (new) clothes, and homes serve **সেমাই**. Children bow to elders and receive **সালামি** — Eid money. **আপু, সালামি দাও!** is a classic line from a younger sibling.

Grammar: **ঈদে** = 'at Eid' (locative), **ঈদের** = 'of Eid' (genitive): **ঈদের দিন** 'on Eid day'.

Millions leave Dhaka for their village homes at Eid — the city goes quiet for days.

sentences.en: At Eid we go to the village.
alt: We go to our village for Eid.
Sister, give me my Eid money.

sentences.en: I will buy new clothes for Eid.
alt: I'll buy a new shirt for Eid.

sentences.bn: ঈদের দিন সকালে আমরা নামাজ পড়ি।
sentences.tr: ider din shokale amra namaj pori.
alt: On the morning of Eid we pray.

lessons.title: Ramadan & iftar
lessons.goal: Talk about fasting, sehri and iftar.
lessons.tip:
During **রমজান** (Ramadan) most Bangladeshi Muslims **রোজা রাখেন** — 'keep the fast' — from dawn to sunset. The verb is **রাখা** 'keep', which you met in the bazaar (**কম রাখেন**!).

The day is framed by two meals: **সেহরি** before dawn and **ইফতার** at sunset. A classic Dhaka iftar: **খেজুর** (dates), ছোলা (chickpeas), পেঁয়াজু (onion fritters), বেগুনি (aubergine fritters) and জিলাপি.

Inviting someone **ইফতারে** ('to iftar') is a big gesture of friendship — non-Muslim friends are warmly welcome.

Note **আপনি কি রোজা রাখেন?** is polite but personal; it's fine between friends.

sentences.bn: আমি সেহরি খাই, তারপর নামাজ পড়ি।
sentences.tr: ami sehri khai, tarpor namaj pori.
sentences.en: I eat sehri, then I pray.
Iftar is at our home today.
alt: Today there's iftar at our house.

sentences.en: It's the month of Ramadan now.

alt: I haven't broken my fast yet.

lessons.title: Pohela Boishakh
grammar: আজ পহেলা বৈশাখ 'today is Pohela Boishakh'
lessons.tip:
**পহেলা বৈশাখ** — the first day of the month Boishakh — is the Bengali New Year, celebrated on **14 April** in Bangladesh by people of every religion. Greet everyone with **শুভ নববর্ষ!** 'Happy New Year!'

Traditions: wearing red and white (লাল-সাদা), the colourful **মঙ্গল শোভাযাত্রা** procession in Dhaka, streets painted with **আলপনা**, a village-style **মেলা** (fair), and a breakfast of **পান্তা ভাত** with ইলিশ.

The pattern **শুভ + occasion** is very productive: **শুভ নববর্ষ**, **শুভ জন্মদিন** (happy birthday), **শুভ সকাল** (good morning, a bit formal).

**Kolkata:** **পয়লা বৈশাখ** (*poyla boishakh*), usually on 14 or 15 April.

sentences.en: Pohela Boishakh is the Bengali New Year.

sentences.bn: আমরা পান্তা ভাত আর ইলিশ খাই।
sentences.tr: amra panta bhat ar ilish khai.
sentences.en: We eat panta bhat and hilsa.
alt: We eat soaked rice and hilsa.

sentences.en: Will you go to the fair?

alt: The floor art is very beautiful.

sentences.en: I will buy a red sari.

lessons.title: Puja
lessons.goal: Talk about Durga Puja and greet Hindu friends.
grammar: শুভ বিজয়া — greeting after Durga Puja
lessons.tip:
About 8% of Bangladeshis are Hindu, and **দুর্গাপূজা** (*durgapuja*) is their biggest **উৎসব** (festival). Thousands of **পূজা মণ্ডপ** (temporary pavilions) are set up across the country, each with a clay **প্রতিমা** of the goddess Durga. Visitors of all faiths go to see them.

On the last day the images are immersed in the river; afterwards friends greet each other with **শুভ বিজয়া** and sweets. With Hindu friends, **নমস্কার** is the natural hello.

In Bangladesh the official slogan is **ধর্ম যার যার, উৎসব সবার** — 'religion is each person's own, festivals belong to everyone'.

**Kolkata:** spoken **পুজো** (*pujo*); Durga Puja is *the* festival of the year.

sentences.en: Durga Puja is a big festival of the Hindus.
alt: Durga Puja is the Hindus' big festival.

sentences.en: At Puja we go to the temple.
alt: During Puja we go to the temple.

sentences.en: I will buy a new sari for Puja.
Eid and Puja are our festivals.

lessons.title: Ekushe & national days
lessons.goal: Understand Language Martyrs' Day, Victory Day and Independence Day.
grammar: X দিবস 'X day'; দিবসে 'on the day'
lessons.tip:
On **21 February 1952**, students in Dhaka were shot while demanding that **বাংলা** be a state language of Pakistan. Bangladesh remembers them on **একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি** — **শহীদ দিবস** (Martyrs' Day). At dawn people walk barefoot to the **শহীদ মিনার** to lay flowers, singing *আমার ভাইয়ের রক্তে রাঙানো একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি*. Since 1999 UNESCO marks the day worldwide as International **Mother Language** (মাতৃভাষা) Day.

Two more national days are public holidays (**ছুটি**):

- **স্বাধীনতা দিবস** — Independence Day, 26 March (1971)
- **বিজয় দিবস** — Victory Day, 16 December (1971)

**দিবস** is the formal word for a named 'Day'; ordinary 'day' is **দিন**.

alt: The twenty-first of February is Martyrs' Day.

sentences.en: In the morning we go to the Shaheed Minar.
Today is Victory Day, we have a holiday.
alt: It's Victory Day today, so we have the day off.
There is a holiday on Independence Day.

lessons.title: Invitations & guests
lessons.goal: Invite people, welcome guests and give gifts.
grammar: future as polite request: আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন 'please come to our home'
আপনাকে 'you' (object); X-এর জন্য / আপনার জন্য 'for X / for you'
lessons.tip:
Bengali invitations use the **future** as a gentle request: **আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন** — literally 'You will come to our home', meaning 'Please do come!' Formally: **আপনাকে দাওয়াত দিলাম** 'I'm inviting you'.

A **মেহমান** (guest) is treated with great honour: expect tea, sweets and **পিঠা**, and to be asked **খাবেন?** more than once. Saying **না** once is often taken as politeness; accept a little.

**জন্য** 'for' follows a genitive: **এই উপহার আপনার জন্য** 'This gift is for you'. Wishes: **শুভ জন্মদিন** 'Happy birthday', **ঈদের শুভেচ্ছা** 'Eid greetings'.

**Kolkata:** নেমন্তন্ন (invitation), অতিথি (guest).

sentences.en: We have guests at home today.
alt: Guests are at our house today.

lessons.title: With close friends
lessons.goal: Use the তুই register naturally with close friends, and suggest 'let's…'.
grammar: 'let's': চল (tui) · চলো (tumi) · চলেন (apni) + present আমি-form: চলো যাই
lessons.tip:
**তুই** is the language of real closeness: best friends, siblings, cousins your age. Among Bangladeshi friends you'll hear **দোস্ত** ('buddy') constantly. Used with a stranger or an elder, তুই is an insult — so only *answer* in তুই once someone uses it with you.

'Let's…' = **চল / চলো / চলেন** + the আমি-form of the verb:

- **চল, মেলায় যাই** (tui) — 'Let's go to the fair'
- **চলো, যাই** (tumi) — 'Let's go'
- **চলেন, চা খাই** (apni) — 'Shall we have tea?'

তুই futures end in **-বি**: **আসবি?** 'Will you come?', **কী খাবি?** 'What'll you have?'

sentences.en: There will be dancing and singing today.
alt: Today there will be dance and music.

lessons.title: Review: festivals & friends
lessons.goal: Greet, invite and celebrate across the year.
grammar: review: festival greetings, invitations, চল/চলো/চলেন, register choice
lessons.tip:
Match the greeting to the occasion:

- Eid — **ঈদ মোবারক**
- Bengali New Year — **শুভ নববর্ষ**
- after Durga Puja — **শুভ বিজয়া**
- birthday — **শুভ জন্মদিন**
- to a whole group — **সবাইকে ঈদের শুভেচ্ছা**

And match the register to the person: **চলেন** with your teacher, **চলো** with a classmate, **চল** with your best friend. When in doubt, go one level *more* polite.

**যদি** "if" + present tense: **যদি সময় হয়** "if there's time" — a soft way to invite.

sentences.en: Please come to our home and have some pitha.

sentences.bn: আজ পহেলা বৈশাখ, চলো মেলায় যাই।
sentences.tr: aj pohela boishakh, cholo melay jai.
sentences.en: Today is Pohela Boishakh, let's go to the fair.

alt: Mate, let's break the fast together.

sentences.bn: একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি আমরা শহীদ মিনার যাই।
sentences.tr: ekushe februari amra shohid minar jai.
sentences.en: On 21 February we go to the Shaheed Minar.

sentences.bn: যদি সময় হয়, আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন।
sentences.tr: jodi shomoy hoy, amader bashay ashben.
sentences.en: If you have time, please come to our home.
alt: If there is time, please come to our place.

sentences.en: There are a lot of people at the fair.
